balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Entain plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Entain plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Entain plc: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Entain plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Entain plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on. Statutory net income was a loss in FY2023 and FY2024 on impairments even as FCF stayed positive; profit for period fills the half-year rows where net income isn't disclosed.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Entain plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Entain plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Entain plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Entain plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

underlyingBridge.title: Underlying vs statutory profit
underlyingBridge.content:
Underlying operating profit is management's adjusted measure (pre-exceptional items, acquisition amortisation and significant legal/regulatory costs). Statutory operating income/loss is the reported figure after those items. Share of JV income is Entain's 50% equity-accounted share of BetMGM; net finance expense paid is cash interest on the group's debt.

For Entain plc: statutory operating income was negative in FY2023 and FY2024 largely on goodwill/intangible impairments (Netherlands, Australia, Ladbrokes legacy), while underlying profit stayed positive throughout -- the two lines tell very different stories about the same business.

What to watch:

  • Whether the underlying/statutory gap is shrinking (fewer exceptionals) or recurring every year
  • Net finance expense trend as leverage (3.1x EBITDA) feeds through to interest cost

segmentNGR.title: Online vs Retail NGR
segmentNGR.content:
NGR (Net Gaming Revenue) is stakes less payouts to customers -- the industry's top line, distinct from statutory revenue which can include other items. Split between Online (digital sportsbook and gaming) and Retail (licensed betting shops, mainly UK/Ireland).

For Entain plc: Online is the larger and faster-growing channel; Retail is the structurally declining shop estate. Disclosed only at the half-year so far.

What to watch:

  • Online NGR growth rate versus Retail's decline
  • Retail's shrinking share of the group mix

segmentEBITDA.title: Online vs Retail EBITDA
segmentEBITDA.content:
Segment EBITDA for the same Online/Retail split, showing where group profit is actually generated rather than just revenue.

For Entain plc: Retail typically carries a higher EBITDA margin on NGR than Online despite its revenue decline, because the shop cost base is largely fixed and already sized down; Online's growth comes with higher marketing and payment costs.

What to watch:

  • Online EBITDA margin trend as marketing spend scales with growth
  • Retail EBITDA holding up as the estate shrinks (operating leverage in reverse)

productMix.title: Sports vs Gaming NGR
productMix.content:
NGR split by product: Sports (sportsbook betting) versus Gaming (online casino, slots, poker).

For Entain plc: Gaming NGR now exceeds Sports NGR and carries a more consistent margin, since it isn't exposed to sports results; Sports NGR depends on both wagering volume and the sports margin (see the wagers chart).

What to watch:

  • Gaming's growing share of the product mix
  • Sports NGR volatility driven by results, not just volume

sportsHold.title: Sports wagers and sports margin
sportsHold.content:
Sports wagers is the total amount staked by customers (turnover) -- much larger than NGR because most stakes are paid back out as winnings. Sports margin is NGR as a percentage of wagers: the average proportion of stakes the bookmaker retains after paying out winners.

For Entain plc: sports margin moves with sporting results (favourites losing lifts it, upsets cut it) independent of any change in customer volume, so a quarter's margin swing is not necessarily a demand signal.

What to watch:

  • Wagers growth as the underlying volume trend
  • Margin reverting toward its historical average rather than one period's print

betmgm.title: BetMGM (US joint venture)
betmgm.content:
BetMGM is the 50/50 US sports-betting and iGaming joint venture with MGM Resorts. Net revenue and adjusted EBITDA are BetMGM's own figures, in US dollars, not GBP like the rest of this dashboard.

For Entain plc: BetMGM's path to sustained profitability in the competitive US market is a major part of the equity story; Entain books its 50% share through Share of JV income (see the underlying-profit bridge chart), not as consolidated revenue.

What to watch:

  • Adjusted EBITDA margin trend as US state-level competition and promotional spend evolve
  • Cash distributions back to the parents (BetMGMCashToParents), once more periods are disclosed

leverage.title: Net debt / EBITDA
leverage.content:
The group's disclosed leverage ratio: net debt (borrowings less cash, as management defines it for covenant purposes, including lease liabilities) divided by EBITDA.

For Entain plc: management has guided toward reducing leverage from the current ~3.1x; this differs from the DCF's own net debt (total debt less cash only), which is a narrower, model-specific figure used purely for the equity bridge.

What to watch:

  • Trend toward or away from the covenant ceiling
  • Whether deleveraging comes from debt paydown or EBITDA growth

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Entain plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
